## Proposed change
<!--

@Drafteed 
> This can also cause a three-fold delay in changing the state when turning off the TV. I think this is a bad attempt to solve the problem caused by the Sony API.

I think this attempt is a proportionate solution to the problem, It's a quick, easy fix to a small, infrequent issue. But if it causes an extra issue of delay, then we clearly need a different solution.

My TV stays connected to WiFi when I turn it off, so in a normal scenario the power state request should successfully return without needing to retry until failure. It would only cause a delay if the status request failed.

I'm not sure whether all Bravia TVs work this way though. I see how it would be a problem if other TVs disconnect from the network immediately on power off - do you know if other Bravia TVs behave this way?

> I'm not sure whether all Bravia TVs work this way though. I see how it would be a problem if other TVs disconnect from the network immediately on power off - do you know if other Bravia TVs behave this way?

Some Bravia TVs lose connection to the network after turning off, for example old TVs without Android/Google TV.

> This can also cause a three-fold delay in changing the state when turning off the TV. I think this is a bad attempt to solve the problem caused by the Sony API.

I don't agree with this comment. The PR adds retry in the coordinator to overcome some API instability which is reasonable.

Setting the TV's state to OFF when we can't reach it seems like a hack on the other hand, I would expect we set the state to unavailable when we can't reach the TV. If really needed, it should probably be enabled only for certain models which disconnect from the network when powered off. Improving that is for a different PR though.

> I would expect we set the state to unavailable when we can't reach the TV

If we set the entity state to unavailable, then we will not be able to [turn on the device via WOL](https://github.com/Drafteed/pybravia/blob/93df39e6358cb38470cf509708a9905de58e1a5d/pybravia/client.py#L530). 

> If really needed, it should probably be enabled only for certain models which disconnect from the network when powered off

I'm almost sure that this is impossible with their API.

> If we set the entity state to unavailable, then we will not be able to turn on the device via WOL

OK, I see.

The TV itself does not power cycle, just the `media_player` entity. This was noticed because of a media bias light that is stuck to the rear of the TV which runs on an automation triggered by the `media_player` state provided by the integration. Has been ongoing for a approximately 2 months now. review_comments: Do we really need to add a new dependency for this?
I don't see this as much of an issue, but yes it could be rewritten to not use tenacity. That being said, tenacity is already a transitive dependency of many of the existing dependencies.
The question is whether such a change should be implemented in the backend library and not in the integration.
Yeah perhaps it should. I noticed that tenacity was included as a dependency in the nibe_heatpump component, and then later moved into the backend library instead.

I don't think this should be done in the backend lib. If we can clearly define the type of error when this happens,, we can use the mechanism that is already implemented here, without using Tenacity. See the code below where the `skipped_updates` counter is used.
I agree we should not introduce an external dependency just to retry, please implement it yourself.
